# Why agents {.divider background-color="#CC0000"}

[What's different, and why it changes the skill]{.eyebrow}

## A chatbot talks. An agent acts.

::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card}
[Chatbot]{.card-title}

- You paste the file in
- It answers in text
- You copy its code out, run it, paste errors back
- **You are its hands**
:::

::: {.card .dark}
[Agent]{.card-title}

- It opens your files itself
- It runs commands and edits files
- It sees its own errors and tries again
- **You steer, and you check**
:::
:::

> "Without tools, Claude can only respond with text. With tools, Claude can act."
> <span class="muted">— Claude Code documentation</span>

## The loop

<div class="loop">
<div class="stage"><b>Read</b>open files, look around</div><div class="arrow">→</div>
<div class="stage"><b>Plan</b>propose before acting</div><div class="arrow">→</div>
<div class="stage"><b>Act</b>edit, run, build</div><div class="arrow">→</div>
<div class="stage"><b>Check</b>is it actually right?</div>
</div>

The docs put it plainly: *"You're part of this loop too."*

::: {.statement style="margin-top:26px"}
The skill now: set it up, *steer* it, *check* it.
:::

## What you're about to install

**Claude Code**: an AI agent that works inside a folder on your computer.

- It can **read and change any file** in the folder you start it in
- You choose how often it asks before acting
- The same agent runs in the terminal, the Desktop app, VS Code and the web

::: {.card .red style="margin-top:22px"}
Think of it as a capable coworker with access to one folder. **Choose the folder on purpose.**
:::
